page_title: Multiclass classification evaluation with ROC Curves and ROC AUC

summary.title: Multiclass classification evaluation with ROC Curves and ROC AUC
summary.one_liner: You learn how to extend the binary ROC curve and ROC AUC metrics to multiclass classification using One-vs-Rest (OvR) and One-vs-One (OvO) strategies.
takeaways: OvR and OvO strategies can adapt any binary classification metric, such as ROC AUC, to multiclass problems.
Plotting per-class histograms and ROC curves (class vs rest) shows how the model separates each class.
OvO evaluates each class pair separately, so 'apple vs banana' and 'banana vs apple' can differ and reveal model inconsistencies.
The average OvO ROC AUC in the fruit example was 0.9409, close to the OvR score of 0.9410.
Per-combination results help find classes the model struggles with and which features to add or remove.
summary.summary: This Towards Data Science article, part of a fruits classification project, explains how to evaluate a multiclass classifier with ROC curves and ROC AUC. It shows how to build One-vs-Rest curves and histograms for each class, then how One-vs-One comparisons handle each pair of classes. It reports an average OvO ROC AUC of 0.9409, close to the OvR result of 0.9410. The text is brief and relies on code snippets whose outputs are shown as images, so the page text does not include the code itself.
